annotations.note: Counter has three transitions (bump, reset, report) and one state field. Textbook minimal single-atom shape. Keep as the canonical demo.
annotations.author: dan

annotations.note: First bump. The guard_eval at seq=4 fired result=1 (true), the arm at seq=5 selected arm=0 at source line 4, the field_write at seq=6 did the increment. The three-event signature (guard_eval → arm → field_write) is the canonical bump footprint. Watch for this pattern in the trace diff view.
annotations.author: dan

annotations.note: The reset arm. n: 2 → 0 at seq=16. If the file-local optimisation ever folds reset into a conditional bump, this range becomes a regression signal — the field_write should still move n from the pre-reset value to exactly 0.
annotations.author: dan

annotations.note: This is NOT a real bug for Counter (report is an observation, not a transition, so no field_write is expected). But if the viewer renders observations as arms-without-side-effects, the diff view needs to visually distinguish an observation arm (one-shot read) from a transition arm (read-then-write) at this trace position. Flagged to inform the viewer's icon palette.
annotations.author: dan
annotations.expected: arm=0 fires, then a `print` or `return` emit event marks the observed-value emission. Current trace emits nothing visible after arm selection.
annotations.actual: arm=0 at line=14 fires. No subsequent field_write or output event in the trace (trace ends at seq=25).

annotations.note: The atom_init edge from CxcMain's init-body to Counter's constructor. Every program has this shape. In the two-commit tween, this edge should be the first thing that stabilises (both commits create a Counter, same ctor-param shape, no delta). Use as a tween anchor point.
